business_problem: CARIAD needed a faster and safer way to validate automated driving functions across large numbers of traffic, weather, and road scenarios, because proving reliability, functional correctness, and regulatory readiness for automated vehicles is difficult with manual or fragmented testing approaches.
solution_summary: CARIAD and DXC built a verification and validation framework to industrialize testing for Volkswagen Group automated driving functions. The framework creates realistic virtual driving scenarios so engineering teams can test how automated systems behave under varied road, traffic, and weather conditions before vehicles reach the road. A domain-specific language called stiEF gives users a natural-language editor for describing scenarios such as stopping at a red light or reacting to sudden lane changes, and the editor translates those descriptions into visual simulations. This lets development and test teams collaborate on the same scenario definitions instead of working through separate specialist workflows. By turning scenario creation and execution into a repeatable digital process, the platform helps CARIAD validate automated driving behavior faster, improve safety confidence, and make regulatory approval work more efficient.

data_flow: Engineers describe driving situations in the stiEF editor using natural language, and the editor converts those inputs into visual simulations. The verification and validation framework then runs the scenarios against automated driving functions under different traffic, weather, and road conditions so CARIAD teams can review safety and functional behavior before release.
business_outcome: CARIAD made automated-driving validation faster and more collaborative, improved confidence that automated systems behave safely across diverse scenarios, and supported more efficient regulatory-approval work for Volkswagen Group automated driving programs.
